newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin blasts U.S. ahead of summit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin blasts U.S. ahead of summit.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin criticised the United States on Monday before this week's summit with Bill Clinton, saying Washington had done little to help post-communist Russia.

Yeltsin said in a television interview, the text of which was released by U.S. network NBC (National Broadcasting Company), that Russia could make no more concessions. "I don't want a return to the Cold War, I don't want it and our people don't want it, but for that there must be equal conditions in the world order," he said.
"Why are anti-dumping limitations in place against Russia?" Yeltsin asked, referring to trade barriers against cheap Russian goods.

Yeltsin is under strong pressure from nationalist and communist opponents not to be seen to take a soft line with Clinton over NATO's plans to expand eastwards -- a topic which is expected to dominate the Helsinki summit starting on Thursday.

Taking a tough line in the interview, he said: "Why, up to now, can Russia not join various world organisations because of U.S. opposition? Why is Russia not recognised as having a market economy yet? Why? Seventy percent is in the private sector."
Yeltsin said other countries with much smaller economies had invested more than the United States in Russia since the collapse of communist rule in 1991.
